name: Baseline: Interpret BRCA1/BRCA2 germline variants
description: Baseline method for the use case, reviewed against its cited sources.

attributes.rationale: The ClinGen ENIGMA BRCA1/BRCA2 specification uses BayesDel, with gene-specific cutpoints, as its computational evidence for missense variants (PP3/BP4), so a new predictor is judged against it. BayesDel is a meta-predictor that combines other scores, so it is a simple trained model rather than a pre-machine-learning method; manual review under the specification, the full comparator, has no method record.

name: Baseline: Transfer cell-type annotations to a new dataset
description: Baseline method for the use case, reviewed against its cited sources.

attributes.value: scmap-cell, linear SVM and logistic regression
attributes.rationale: Manual marker-based annotation, the pre-machine-learning practice, has no method record, so the simplest measured comparators are named instead: nearest-reference projection (scmap-cell) and linear classifiers trained on labelled expression. Abdelaal et al. 2019 found the linear SVM the best performer overall among 22 methods, and scTab uses a tuned logistic regression as its reference model.

name: Baseline: Select a patient-RNA splicing-variant validation workflow
description: Baseline method for the use case, reviewed against its cited sources.

attributes.value: FRASER and OUTRIDER, with a legacy splice-site vote
attributes.rationale: On patient RNA, FRASER (splicing) and OUTRIDER (expression) are the standard outlier callers, run in the DROP workflow; they fit count models to the cohort and are not trained on labelled variants. On DNA, the reference is the Legacy Ensemble, a vote across MaxEntScan, NNSplice, GeneSplicer and a SpliceSiteFinder-style matrix; NNSplice is an early neural network, so this vote is a legacy comparator rather than a strictly pre-machine-learning one.
